38304-encyclopaedia-britannica-11th-edit:
Britannica eleventh edition volume here runs from Groups, Theory of, onward. Articles treat the Guadalquivir river and Guanajuato mining town in range. Guarantee law under Egyptian codes gets a careful legal entry. Guinea fowl kinds and Guipúzcoa crafts fill shorter pieces here.

The volume is one slice of the great 1910 to 1911 reference set. Entries run from mathematics to place names in strict letter order. Irun, Eibar, and other Basque towns appear for their arms trade. Scholars of the day wrote the signed articles in the set. Cotton and linen towns of the province fill one more industrial note in the entries.
podcast-dannyjones-pt5CbCTmAgw:
Harvard astronomer Avi Loeb joins Danny Jones to say he thinks aliens may be trying to reach us. Loeb is a top space scientist known for his hunt for alien tech near Earth. He argues the search should be bold and open.

Loeb talks about odd space rocks, signals, and the case for craft from other stars. He faults his peers for fear of the topic. Jones asks what find would prove him right once and for all. Listeners get the case from the best known name in the field. The library holds the talk as an archive record.
